subject: Private tenancy cutover: proposed schedule & risk matrix
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Elyse Chen <elyse@acmehealth.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 09 Sep 2026 09:17:00 -0700
Subject: Private tenancy cutover: proposed schedule & risk matrix

Hi Elyse / team —

Following our site call last week, attached is a first-pass plan for the tenancy cutover we discussed (move from shared-hosted to VPC/private tenancy). High level: we want a staged, limited-impact cutover with clear rollback gates. Attachments: vpc-tenancy-cutover-risk-matrix.xlsx (detailed risks & mitigations), proposed-cutover-windows.ics (three candidate windows), rollback-play-quick-reference.pdf (ops playbook).

Key asks from Acme:
- Confirm which of the three candidate windows works for your operations and procurement timelines.
- Any blackout dates or fiscal constraints we should avoid (billing/maintenance windows).
- Approval for our proposed short DR test window on the dry-run day (we'll simulate traffic redirection for 30 min).

Risk summary (short):
- Data plane: KV cache warmup latency on first traffic after cutover — mitigation: warmup traffic + canary routing.
- Authentication: customer SAML metadata mismatch risk — mitigation: pre-cutover SAML validation window.
- Networking: eBPF iptables changes at layer-2 during cutover — mitigation: staged subnet drain + NOC monitor.

I've cc'd Neha for procurement alignment and Karthik to scope the network ops schedule. Soojin will own the rollback playbook if we need to evacuate.

Proposed next step: pick a preferred window and we’ll lock a pre-cutover dry-run two business days prior.

Thanks,
Rishi
Director, Customer Engineering
Redwood Inference

Date: Thu, 10 Sep 2026 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private tenancy cutover: proposed schedule & risk matrix

Thanks Rishi — I reviewed the attachments with our infra and procurement teams this morning. A few items from Acme side:

1) Windows: the "candidate B" evening window (UTC 02:00-04:00) is the only one that doesn't conflict with our nightly batch jobs, so that's our preference, assuming the dry-run can be scheduled earlier in the same week.

2) Procurement: we need a finalized SOW and a brief MOP (step-by-step) to attach to our change request. Can you provide a one-page MOP summary and an SOW addendum that lists the maintenance window and rollback SLA? Procurement flagged that they need the PO cutoff three business days before the window.

3) Rollback clarity: we don't want more than a single, automated rollback attempt without manual signoff. Can you confirm the decision gates and the estimated time-to-restore in your playbook?

I'll hold the preferred window tentatively until we get the MOP and SOW addendum.

—Elyse
VP, Cloud Operations
Acme Health
[Procurement asked for: SOW addendum, 1-page MOP]

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Elyse Chen <elyse@acmehealth.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 11 Sep 2026 08:43:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private tenancy cutover: proposed schedule & risk matrix

Elyse — thanks for the quick review and clear asks. Below are concrete answers and next deliverables.

A) Window: we’ll tentatively lock candidate B (UTC 02:00-04:00) pending PO. Dry-run: propose Wed two days prior, 02:00-02:45 UTC (30-minute dry-run + 15-minute retro).

B) SOW / MOP: Neha — I'm handing off to you for the SOW addendum and the 1-page MOP. Can you confirm you can deliver by end of day Monday (2026-09-13) so Elyse's procurement team can start the PO clock?

C) Rollback gates (summary from ops playbook):
- Gate A (pre-cutover): network sanity and SAML health checks pass — auto-proceed.
- Gate B (canary traffic): if error-rate > 1% for 10 minutes across canary, we pause and escalate.
- Gate C (post-cutover): if sustained tail-latency > 2x baseline for 20 minutes, automatic rollback will trigger one automated evacuation of new tenancy and restore traffic to shared-hosted fleet. After one auto-rollback, manual signoff from Acme ops (Elyse or delegate) required to attempt a second cutover.

Estimated time-to-restore (after automated rollback): 18–30 minutes (typical):
- Traffic reroute: 6–10 min
- KV cache cold restore to acceptable QPS: 8–12 min
- Health-check resync: 4–8 min

Soojin — ops will own the evacuation steps. Karthik, please confirm the network drain script and whether we need any special BGP prep from Acme's side (prewarming routes).

Rishi
Director, Customer Engineering
Redwood Inference
